title: סבב שני: עולם חזותי אימרסיבי עם שני מצבים
question: ההגרלה בחרה ב'רכיבה על רצועת מביוס'. אפשר לשמור אותה, לבחור חלופה, או להגריל שוב.

options.label: רצועת מביוס
options.lineage: The Möbius strip: the mathematical surface with one side and one edge
options.thesis: The whole site is one Möbius band in 3D. Scrolling rides the camera along it from station to station, and one lap brings you back 'on the other side' of the same surface.
materials: black type printed on the band
options.viewport: Name and ShoobyD set large on cobalt beside a twisting white band; the first station (SD-01) is printed on the band, the stations ahead appear as ghosts, a station track runs at the bottom, and there's a 'game mode' button.
options.risk: A 3D band with text stuck to a twisting surface hurts readability, so the text has to be DOM that the camera stops in front of. The math metaphor can feel cold without the humor.

raised.raise: Scrolling moves in whole stations: the band steps from station to station with a small overshoot and never parks half-way.
Stations you haven't visited are drawn on the band as ghosts, so the whole route is always visible and each one lights up when you reach it.
A fixed state vocabulary for every project (live, archive, closed), readable at a glance on every station.
Every station carries a dated label: year, technology and status, like a jar label with harvest and day count.
A signature stripe printed along the band's edge identifies the site (and the sibling repos) before any word.

options.label: מגדל בבל ספירלי
options.lineage: The Tower of Babel as painted by Bruegel, an ascending ramp of tiers
options.thesis: Scrolling climbs a spiral tower; each tier is one of his worlds (code, math, languages, music, drawing), and projects are rooms set into the ramp.
options.viewport: The tower rising from the bottom of the screen with the name at the upper corner; the camera starts at the base and climbs as you scroll. The game mode is 'build a tier'.
options.risk: A famous image that can become a painted illustration rather than a working interface; the biblical imagery may read heavy. It's also the obvious answer for 'languages + Bible'.

options.label: שילוט טרמינל
options.thesis: The site as a concourse: a yellow overhead sign at every junction, and projects as gates with status.
options.viewport: Two yellow bands at the top pointing to the projects and to contact, the name large in the hall, and a departures board of projects.
options.case: Holds product clarity: wayfinding is exactly the goal of 'two audiences find their path'. Loses identification, because an airport isn't him, and it's flatter than the 3D you asked for.
options.risk: Clever but impersonal, and bilingual signage is already a cliché in airports.

options.label: מדף זיגוג בכבשן
options.lineage: Kiln shelves of glaze test cups
options.thesis: Each project is a cup whose glaze runs down.
options.viewport: A row of cups on a shelf.
options.case: Fuses poorly: ceramics isn't one of his worlds, and it doesn't introduce a person.
options.risk: A beautiful craft that isn't his.
options.kept: A fixed state vocabulary (dry, melting, running, pooled), now project statuses.

options.label: לוח כבישה
options.thesis: Every interest is a jar that ripens over time.
options.case: Fuses partly: cooking is a hobby of his, but it pulls the whole site into the kitchen, and it isn't 3D-immersive.
options.kept: A dated label on every item, so every station has a year, technology and status.

options.label: גלילת יעד של אוטובוס
options.lineage: Cloth destination blinds in old buses
options.thesis: Content rides a roll of cloth under a fixed window.
options.viewport: One fixed window with a destination in it.
options.case: Fuses poorly: it's a world built for monitoring screens, and it doesn't introduce a person.
options.kept: Moving in whole steps with a small overshoot, so the scroll steps station by station.

options.label: תצוגת שבעה מקטעים
options.lineage: Seven-segment displays: alarm clocks and scoreboards
options.thesis: Everything written in one eight-cell mask.
options.case: Fuses poorly: Hebrew isn't written in seven segments, and it's cheap nostalgia.
options.kept: Absence designed too (ghost cells), so unvisited stations stay visible as ghosts.

options.label: מוסך מרוצי סיבולת
options.thesis: The site as a race car with stripes and a number roundel.
options.viewport: A car in the garage under sodium light.
options.case: Fuses poorly: racing isn't his, and it's too close to Bruno Simon's car.
options.risk: An imitation of a famous portfolio.
options.kept: A stripe system that identifies before any word, as a signature stripe along the band's edge.

canonCard.label: פורטפוליו תלת־ממדי סטנדרטי
canonCard.thesis: The category standard for immersive portfolios: a dark scene, one glossy floating object, a scroll-driven camera, big type.
canonCard.viewport: A large headline beside a glowing 3D sphere, with 'SCROLL ↓' at the bottom.
canonCard.risk: Looks like a hundred other 3D portfolios: impressive but not his.
